nodes.title: A fresh clone has no pre-push gate: core.hooksPath is unset, so the 16-leg preflight silently does not run
nodes.description:
**BLUF: a working copy cloned from GitHub has NO pre-push gate.** `core.hooksPath` **is unset in a fresh clone,** `.git/hooks/pre-push` **does not exist there, so the 16-leg preflight does not run — silently. The push just succeeds. A worktree off the shared checkout inherits the gate; a clone does not.**

## Measured 2026-10-19, read-only `git config --get core.hooksPath`

| working copy | `core.hooksPath` | gate runs? |
| -- | -- | -- |
| the shared checkout `2_Project_Files` | `.githooks` | yes |
| a worktree off it (`worktrees/s-r46-ks1462`) | `.githooks` (inherited) | yes |
| a fresh `git clone` from GitHub | **UNSET** | **NO** |
| `deploy-clones/seatC25-7e2f8157cec2` (a live seat's clone at the time) | **UNSET** | **NO** |

`.githooks/pre-push` is present and executable in the clone — it is simply never invoked, because nothing points git at it.

## Why this is worth a ticket rather than a note

**The failure is silent and it looks like success.** A push from an unwired clone prints no warning and no leg output; it prints the ordinary "new branch" line. There is nothing in the output that says the gate was skipped, so the only way to notice is to know the leg headers should be there and see that they are not.

**It happened, on this ticket's own session.** Seat E 3rd's first push of the KS-1195 branch ran with no gate. It was rejected by the remote for an unrelated reason — the branch name collided with a stale 17-September branch — so nothing landed and no ungated commit exists. Had the name been free, an ungated push would have succeeded and been reported as pushed. That is luck, not a control.

**It is already documented**, at `Blockchain/Dev/CONTRIBUTING.md:389`:
`git config core.hooksPath .githooks && chmod +x .githooks/pre-push`
So this is a missable step, not an undocumented hole. The problem is that missing it is undetectable from the push's own output.

## Fix shapes (not chosen here)

1. **Make the absence loud rather than the wiring mandatory.** A tracked `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/*` check, or a preflight leg, that refuses when `core.hooksPath` does not resolve to `.githooks` — this cannot help the very push it would gate, so it only helps on the *second* push onward.
2. **A** `postinstall` **/ bootstrap step** that sets `core.hooksPath` when it is unset. `npm ci` is `ignore-scripts` in this repo, so a postinstall would not fire; it would have to hang off an existing bootstrap script the seats already run.
3. **Have the launcher wire it for every working copy it knows about**, including `deploy-clones/*`, rather than relying on the clone inheriting anything.
4. **A server-side ruleset** that refuses a push without the evidence the hook produces. The strongest, and the most work; also note "Require status checks" must never be enabled while Actions are retired, so this would need to be something other than a check.

Shape 1 or 3 looks like the cheapest honest improvement; the decision is not mine.

## Reproduce

```
git clone --single-branch --branch develop git@github.com:Secuura/Distributed_Secuura.git /tmp/probe
git -C /tmp/probe config --get core.hooksPath   # prints nothing, exit 1
ls /tmp/probe/.git/hooks/pre-push               # No such file or directory
```

Discovered 2026-10-19 by Seat E 3rd during the KS-1195 build (PR #1613), after the push log showed zero leg output.
